body.statement:
There are constants \(C_B,C_S,C_G\), depending only on \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L_\pi,L_\mu,L_\tau)\) and the fixed basis normalizations, such that for every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), every \(0<h\le r_0\), and every finite integer \(k\ge1\) with \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\), the projected private pilots satisfy the same H\"older-radius and range restrictions as the primitive nuisances and
\[
 \Pr_Q\!\left\{\left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)\right|>
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\right\}\le\eta.
\]
The three displayed summands respectively bound localization plus higher-order nuisance bias, sampling fluctuation of the linear and degenerate terms, and all propagated Gaussian release noise.  No rank condition relating \(k\) to \(m h^d\) is required.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), \(0<h\le r_0\), a finite integer \(k\ge1\), and deterministic pilot dimensions \(J_\pi,J_\mu\ge1\), and condition on the two pilot releases.  By Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\), the true nuisances belong to the nonempty closed convex sets \(\mathcal C_\pi\) and \(\mathcal C_\mu\), using Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}overlap}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}propensity\text{-}holder}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}control\text{-}holder}\).  Hence the metric projections \(\bar\pi\) and \(\bar\mu\) lie in those sets.  In particular, their ranges and H\"older radii equal the restrictions required by Lemmas \(\mathrm{lem{:}localized\text{-}spline\text{-}population\text{-}algebra}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}localized\text{-}score\text{-}concentration\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\), uniformly in the realized Gaussian pilot noises.

Put \(\ell=h/k^{1/d}\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}localized\text{-}spline\text{-}population\text{-}algebra}\) supplies \(\vartheta_\tau\in\mathbb R^{p_\gamma}\) such that
\[
 \rho_h(x_0)^{\mathsf T}\vartheta_\tau=\tau_Q(x_0),
 \qquad \|\vartheta_\tau\|_2\le C,
\tag{1}
\]
and, writing \((Q^\circ,R^\circ)=\mathbb E_Q[(T_{*,Q},T_{*,R})\mid\bar\pi,\bar\mu]\),
\[
 \|R^\circ-Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau\|_2\le Cb_0,
 \qquad
 \|Q^\circ-Q^0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\ell^{2\alpha},
\tag{2}
\]
where
\[
 b_0=h^\gamma+\ell^{\alpha+\beta}+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(Q^0)\ge\lambda_0:=\kappa(1-\kappa),
 \qquad
 \|R^\circ\|_2\le C.
\tag{3}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}overlap}\) and \(0<\kappa<1/2\) give \(\lambda_0>0\).  Also \(0<\ell\le h\le r_0\), since \(k\ge1\).

Let
\[
 x_\eta=\log(8/\eta),\qquad M_h=mh^d,
\]
and define
\[
 a_0=
 \sqrt{\frac{x_\eta}{M_h}\left(1+\frac{k}{M_h}\right)}
 +\frac{x_\eta}{M_h}
 +\frac{\sqrt{k}\,x_\eta^{3/2}}{M_h^{3/2}}
 +\frac{kx_\eta^2}{M_h^2},
\tag{4}
\]
\[
 g_0=\frac{\sqrt{\log(1/\delta_n)x_\eta}}{m\epsilon_n}
       \{h^{-d}+kh^{-2d}\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Choose \(C_S\ge\sqrt{C_0}\), where \(C_0\) is the constant in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}localized\text{-}score\text{-}concentration\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\).  The hypothesis \(M_h\ge C_S^2x_\eta\) then implies \(M_h\ge C_0x_\eta\), so that lemma yields, conditionally on the pilots, an event \(E_S\) with
\[
 \Pr_Q(E_S\mid\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\ge1-\eta/2,
 \qquad
 \|T_*-T_*^\circ\|_2\le C a_0
 \quad\hbox{on }E_S.
\tag{6}
\]
This application is valid for every finite \(k\); no comparison between \(k\) and \(M_h\) is used.

The Gaussian vector in the main-block release has the fixed dimension
\(D_*=p_\gamma^2+p_\gamma\).  For a scalar standard normal \(Z\), completing
the square in its density gives, for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \mathbb E e^{tZ}
 =(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-z^2/2+tz}\,dz
 =e^{t^2/2}.
\]
Markov's inequality with \(t=u\), applied also to \(-Z\), therefore gives
\(\Pr\{|Z|>u\}\le2e^{-u^2/2}\).  Since
\(\|Z_*\|_2\le\sqrt{D_*}\max_j|Z_{*,j}|\), a coordinate union bound with
\(u=\sqrt{2\log(4D_*/\eta)}\) yields
\[
 \Pr\{\|Z_*\|_2>\sqrt{2D_*\log(4D_*/\eta)}\}\le\eta/2.
\]
The dimension \(D_*\) depends only on \(d\) and \(\gamma\), and
\(0<\eta<1/4\), so \(\log(4D_*/\eta)\le C\log(8/\eta)=Cx_\eta\).
Consequently,
\[
 \Pr\{\|Z_*\|_2>C\sqrt{x_\eta}\}\le\eta/2.
\tag{7}
\]
The declared parameter ranges \(0<\delta_n<1/2\), \(0<\epsilon_n\le1\), and the definitions of \(c_{\delta_n}\) and \(\epsilon_n^\circ\) imply
\[
 c_{\delta_n}\le C\sqrt{\log(1/\delta_n)},
 \qquad
 (\epsilon_n^\circ)^{-1}\le2\epsilon_n^{-1}.
\tag{8}
\]
The unchanged sensitivity conclusion of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}private\text{-}release\text{-}and\text{-}sensitivity}\), together with (7)--(8) and the Gaussian scale in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\), therefore gives an event \(E_G\) such that
\[
 \Pr(E_G\mid\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\ge1-\eta/2,
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde T_*-T_*\|_2\le Cg_0
 \quad\hbox{on }E_G.
\tag{9}
\]
Consequently, on \(E=E_S\cap E_G\), the union bound gives conditional probability at least \(1-\eta\), and the componentwise reconstruction of \((\widetilde Q,\widetilde R)\), (6), and (9) give
\[
 \|\widetilde Q-Q^\circ\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\|\widetilde R-R^\circ\|_2
 \le e_0:=C(a_0+g_0).
\tag{10}
\]

We first consider the stable case
\[
 C\ell^{2\alpha}+e_0\le\lambda_0/2,
\tag{11}
\]
where the constant is enlarged, if necessary, to be the one in (2).  For every unit vector \(v\), (2), (3), and (10) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\widetilde Qv\|_2
 &\ge \|Q^0v\|_2
      -\|(Q^\circ-Q^0)v\|_2
      -\|(\widetilde Q-Q^\circ)v\|_2\\
 &\ge\lambda_0-C\ell^{2\alpha}-e_0
 \ge\lambda_0/2.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
Thus \(\sigma_{\min}(\widetilde Q)\ge\lambda_0/2>\lambda_0/4\).  The singular-value floor in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\) is inactive, so \(\widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}=\widetilde Q\) and
\[
 \|\widetilde Q^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/\lambda_0.
\tag{13}
\]
Using (1), inserting and subtracting \(R^\circ\), \(Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau\), and \(\widetilde Q\vartheta_\tau\), and then applying (2), (10), (13), and the fixed bound on \(\rho_h(x_0)\), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)|
 &\le \|\rho_h(x_0)\|_2\|\widetilde Q^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
       \|\widetilde R-\widetilde Q\vartheta_\tau\|_2\\
 &\le C\bigl(
       \|R^\circ-Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau\|_2
       +\|\widetilde R-R^\circ\|_2
       +\|\widetilde Q-Q^\circ\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|\vartheta_\tau\|_2
       \bigr)\\
 &\le C(b_0+a_0+g_0).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]

If (11) fails, then either \(C\ell^{2\alpha}>\lambda_0/4\) or \(e_0>\lambda_0/4\).  In the first alternative, positivity of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) yields
\[
 \ell^{\alpha+\beta}
 =\left(\ell^{2\alpha}\right)^{(\alpha+\beta)/(2\alpha)}
 \ge c_1>0;
\tag{15}
\]
in the second, \(a_0+g_0\ge c_2>0\).  Hence in either alternative
\[
 b_0+a_0+g_0\ge c_*>0.
\tag{16}
\]
The singular-value floor always gives
\(\|\widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le4/\lambda_0\).  By (3) and (10), \(\|\widetilde R\|_2\le C+e_0\); moreover \(|\tau_Q(x_0)|\le1\) by the range in the definition of \(\tau_Q\).  Therefore, on \(E\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)|
 &\le \|\rho_h(x_0)\|_2
       \|\widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
       \|\widetilde R\|_2+|\tau_Q(x_0)|\\
 &\le C(1+a_0+g_0)
 \le C'(b_0+a_0+g_0),
 \end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
where (16) justifies the last inequality.

Choose \(C_B,C_S,C_G\) at least as large as the constants in (14) and (17), while retaining \(C_S\ge\sqrt{C_0}\).  Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}bias\text{-}envelope}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}sampling\text{-}envelope}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}privacy\text{-}envelope}\) then give
\[
 B(h,k)=C_Bb_0,\qquad
 S(h,k,\eta)=C_Sa_0,\qquad
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)=C_Gg_0.
\tag{18}
\]
Equations (14), (17), and (18) prove the asserted raw-estimator error inequality on \(E\).  Its conditional failure probability is at most \(\eta\), uniformly over the realized pilots and every finite \(k\); integration over both pilot blocks proves the unconditional assertion, including all pilot and main-block Gaussian randomness.  Finally, clipping the released center in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\) is downstream post-processing and does not enter this lemma: the controlled object throughout is the unchanged raw estimator \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)\).
body.justification: The uniform raw-estimator envelope controls localization bias, higher-order nuisance bias, sampling fluctuation, and Gaussian release noise before any center clipping; downstream projection leaves this proof unchanged.
body.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 gives an expected-error decomposition without privacy or coverage; ArmstrongKolesar2020 treats worst-case smoothing bias without causal higher-order nuisance bias.
body.consumer: The bound gives investigators a finite-sample radius that remains valid when low nuisance smoothness makes first-order CATE intervals undercover.
